## Sessions and rates

- **Single session** — $140, 75 to 90 minutes. Suitable as a first visit, as
  targeted work on one complaint, or as a tune-up.
- **Short series** — 3 or 5 sessions at $140 each, usually spaced one to three
  weeks apart. The most common choice.
- **The Ten Series** — the classical Rolfing recipe, 10 to 12 sessions at $140
  each, working through the whole structure layer by layer.

Sessions are self-pay. Some clients use HSA or FSA funds or submit a receipt to
their plan.

## What Rolfing® Structural Integration is

Rolfing Structural Integration is hands-on bodywork that reorganizes fascia, the
connective tissue that wraps every muscle, bone and organ. Rather than treating
symptoms where they are felt, it looks at how the whole body is organized in
gravity and works on the holding patterns that keep pulling a person back into
pain.

It differs from massage in aim rather than technique. Massage generally targets
relaxation and relief in the moment. Rolfing targets structure, follows a plan
across sessions, and includes movement education so changes hold.

Commonly sought for chronic back, neck, hip and shoulder pain, posture, recovery
from injury, and restoring range of movement.

## Common questions

- **Does Rolfing hurt?** It can be intense in places but should not be something
  a client grits their teeth through. Pressure ranges from light, listening
  contact to firm and deliberate, adjusted continuously on client feedback.
- **How many sessions are needed?** A specific, recent complaint can often be
  addressed in one to three sessions. Longer-standing patterns usually call for
  a series of three, five, or the full ten.
- **What should a client wear?** Comfortable clothing that allows movement, such
  as running shorts and a sports bra or fitted athletic wear, since part of the
  session involves standing and walking.
- **Is insurance accepted?** No. Sessions are self-pay.
